title: Universal test and negated existential test
statement: Let $l$ be a list of natural numbers and let $p,q$ be Boolean-valued functions on the natural numbers. If $p(a)$ is the negation of $q(a)$ for every entry $a$ of $l$, then every entry of $l$ satisfies $p$ exactly when no entry of $l$ satisfies $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $l$ is a list of natural numbers
$p,q$ are Boolean-valued functions on the natural numbers
